conversation_history.utterance: Teacher (Dr. Sharma): Great question, Noah! Beam search is a decoding strategy used during text generation to balance creativity and coherence. Instead of choosing the single most likely next token at each step (which can lead to repetitive or overly safe text), beam search keeps track of multiple candidate sequences—called beams—simultaneously. It explores several possible next tokens and their probabilities, maintaining the top sequences with the highest overall likelihood. This allows the model to consider alternative paths that might be less probable locally but lead to more coherent and contextually rich sentences globally. By adjusting the beam width—the number of sequences tracked—beam search can control the trade-off between creativity (exploring diverse options) and coherence (sticking to the most probable paths). This balance helps generate text that is both fluent and interesting, avoiding dull or nonsensical outputs.
